metadata.name: zip
metadata.description: Create and manage ZIP archive files

installation.note: zip is installed by default on most Linux distributions

overview.summary: zip creates ZIP archive files, compressing and bundling multiple files into a single archive. ZIP is a widely supported format, compatible with Windows, macOS, and Linux. Essential for creating backups, sharing files, and organizing multiple files into single archives.

syntax.description: Create ARCHIVE.zip containing FILES. Can include multiple files and directories. Use -r for directories.

examples.title: Create ZIP archive

breakdown.progress: Shows each file as it's added

breakdown.compression: Shows how much file was compressed
breakdown.percentage: 45% means file is 45% smaller in archive

output_explanation.notes: Shows files being added and compression ratio. Archive created with specified files.

examples.use_case: Create ZIP archives with multiple files

examples.title: Create archive with directory
examples.output: (shows all files in directory being added)

elements.meaning: Recursive - includes directory and all contents

output_explanation.notes: Creates archive with entire directory. -r is essential for directories. Shows all files being added.

breakdown.tradeoff: Better compression = smaller file but slower
breakdown.useful: Use for final archives, sharing files

output_explanation.notes: Creates archive with maximum compression. Slower but creates smaller files. Use for final archives.

examples.title: Exclude files

breakdown.useful: Exclude temporary files, logs, build artifacts

output_explanation.notes: Creates archive excluding specified patterns. Very useful for excluding logs, temp files, node_modules, etc.

examples.use_case: Create archives excluding specific files (logs, temp files)

misconceptions.title: zip and tar are the same
misconceptions.reality: zip compresses and archives in one step. tar only archives (use with gzip for compression). zip is more common on Windows, tar on Linux.
misconceptions.tip: zip = compress + archive. tar = archive only (use tar.gz for compression). zip is cross-platform, tar is Linux standard.

common_pitfalls.description: zip doesn't include directory contents without -r
common_pitfalls.solution: Always use zip -r for directories. Without -r, only directory name is added, not contents.

related_commands.relationship: Archive; tar for Linux standard, zip for cross-platform
related_commands.description: Create archives (Linux standard, use tar.gz for compression)

best_practices: Use zip -9 for maximum compression when size matters
Use zip -x to exclude files (logs, temp files, node_modules)
performance_tips: zip compression speed depends on level (-0 fast, -9 slow)
Use -0 for fast archiving without compression

additional_notes.compression_levels: 0 = no compression (fast), 9 = best compression (slow). Default is 6.
additional_notes.vs_tar: zip = compress + archive, cross-platform. tar = archive only (use tar.gz), Linux standard.
additional_notes.common_patterns: Very common: zip archive.zip files (create), zip -r archive.zip dir/ (directory), zip -r project.zip . -x 'node_modules/*' (exclude)
